text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a 20-30% regression in tail P99 on the mixed-precision rollout when we enable per-layer 4-bit quant with embedding/lm_head excluded. Regression only shows up for short sequences and when KV hits are >60% :thinking_face:

sophia: ugh, saw that locally too. can you paste the perf trace?

maya: Pasting the top of a perf summary from perf-bot run: 
```
Model: custom-13B (layerwise 4bit, exclude=[0, -1])
HW: A100 40GB, CUDA 12.2
Profile (sampled):
  aten::matmul (fused_mha)             42.7%
  quantize_forward (pack/quant kernels) 18.3%
  dequantize (unpack)                  11.2%
  kv_cache_copy                         8.9%
  cudaMemcpy / dtype conversions       6.4%
  other (softmax, gelu, overhead)      12.5%
Total tokens/sec: 1123  (baseline FP16: 1490)
```

raj: that kv_cache_copy number jumps out. when we partially quantize, we still store KV in FP16 by default, and we end up converting on every cache hit for the quantized layers. extra memcpy + dequant kills short seq p99.

oliver: confirm — for fully quantized run we have fewer conversions because kernels already take quantized inputs. partial quantization forces mixed-dtype shims.

kevin: any evidence kernel selection is choosing a fallback non-fused matmul? those would be bad for small batches.

sophia: yes, saw this in kernel log: 
```
[2026-02-24 14:12:04] kernel_selector: chosen kernel: matmul_general (no-fp8-fused) for layer 3
[2026-02-24 14:12:04] kernel_selector: chosen kernel: matmul_fused_fp8 for layer 8
```
layer 3 is one of the "sensitive" layers we quantized to 4-bit in the config (we excluded embeddings but not a few middle layers). kernel selector picks different kernels per-layer which fragments execution pattern.

maya: so two problems: (1) dtype conversion overhead on KV cache hits, (2) kernel fragmentation reducing amortization across batches. both explain p99 for short seqs.

eva: I ran a quick microbench to isolate KV overhead. command: 
```bash
python perf/bench.py --model custom-13B --mode forward --quant 4bit --exclude-layers 0,-1 --seq-len 16 --batch-dist zipf --kv-hit-rate 0.7 --profile
```
output snippet: 
```
KV hit path avg latency: 3.8ms (FP16 baseline: 1.1ms)
quant/dequant overhead per hit: ~1.7ms
memcpy time: 0.9ms
```

raj: calibration note — our current 4-bit calibration uses per-tensor symmetric minmax. that lowers accuracy variance but increases range and forces more aggressive kernel choices. per-channel asymmetric calibration shrinks quant range for attention proj layers and seems to reduce dequant churn because fewer values saturate and we can reuse fused kernels.

kevin: interesting — so calibration affects not just quality but also which kernel we select because of kernel compatibility constraints (e.g., kernel_fused_fp8 requires per-channel scales).

oliver: propose short-term mitigations: 
- treat KV cache as canonical dtype -> always store in the dtype of the most common downstream kernel (prefer FP16 or int8 packed format)
- add a runtime fast-path that avoids dequant on hits by storing both packed and unpacked pointers for hot KV shards
- improve kernel selection cost model to prefer homogeneous kernels across adjacent layers when batch size small

sophia: I prototyped the second idea (store packed + unpacked) as a toggle. perf diff: 
```
Before: tokens/sec 1123 / p99 58ms
After:  tokens/sec 1360 / p99 22ms
Memory overhead: ~12% for KV (can be gated per-customer)
```

maya: that looks promising. any caveats?

sophia: yes — increased memory and extra complexity for eviction. also need to be careful with multi-tenant memory accounting in Dedicated.

eva: batching heuristics note — our dynamic batching window currently greedily merges small requests to fill 1024 token budget. with mixed per-layer kernels, merging requests from different routing decisions causes kernel selector churn (different preferred kernels per-request). for short-seq p99 we should prefer affinity-based batching (group by model-quant-config + layer-compatibility).

raj: agrees. added a quick patch to the batching policy pseudocode: 
```python
# in batcher
group_key = (model_id, quant_profile_hash, kernel_compat_mask)
add_to_group(group_key, req)
if group_ready(group_key): flush(group_key)
```
This reduced kernel churn in my local trace.

kevin: action items?

maya: I'll open a perf PR with the KV packed-cache toggle behind a feature flag. sophia can add the batching affinity change to a separate PR. raj will run a calibration sweep to compare per-tensor vs per-channel for sensitive layers. eva will run Dedicated memory impact analysis.

oliver: can we get an automated regression test? perf-bot should run the bench scenario with kv-hit 0.7 and seq-len 16 nightly.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly job `mixed-quant-p99-shortseq` (runs on a100-nightly). will post diff when available. :robot_face:

maya: thanks all. let's aim to land the toggle + batching change this week and iterate on calibration next. feel free to DM if you need help with infra for the memory accounts. :thumbsup:

sophia: adding notes to the runbook about per-layer exclusion heuristics: prefer excluding first 2 layers and final LM head as default; mark middle layers for per-channel calibration if they are attention-heavy.

kevin: nice. also add a small doc blurb about how calibration choices influence kernel selection — helped me reason about tradeoffs.

maya: closing loop — will update thread with PR numbers.

maya: (follow-up) PRs: #4023 (kv-packed-cache toggle), #4027 (batching affinity).
